summary: The second SDD session loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and made a new worktree. It registered on the plan, and `next` reported Task 2 as the only claimable task. It claimed Task 2 right away, then implemented, reviewed and merged it into feature/parallel (e7dd1cf). It handed back with Task 3 waiting on Task 1, which fixture-session holds. It never tried to take Task 1 over and never stopped or asked about Task 1 before claiming Task 2.
reasoning: All five criteria are backed by the session JSONL and the progress.md ledger. The skill loaded first; register and next ran, and next returned tasks=2; Task 2 was claimed with --session and completed, and the ledger has its branch line; no Bash command contains --takeover; and nothing stopped the run or asked about Task 1 between next and the claim. The guard's false positive on the word 'parallel' is a real issue in the environment, but the agent got past it by using commit SHAs, and it does not affect the held-task behavior this scenario tests.

observations.description: Claude Code's worktree safety guard seems to treat the word 'parallel' in the branch name feature/parallel as the GNU `parallel` tool. It blocked git commands such as `git switch --detach feature/parallel`, and the agent had to detach by SHA (46be16d) instead. Several compound commands were also refused as 'too complex to verify', so the agent re-ran register/verify/deps/next as separate commands.

EnterWorktree made a branch named worktree-feature-parallel-6ba3c913. The agent then tried to delete it while the worktree was still checked out on it and got 'error: cannot delete branch ... used by worktree'. The worktree branch handling was clumsy.

Startup prompts: the folder trust dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog both have 'No, exit' selected by default. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5, and the header then showed Opus 5.5. I chose 'No'.

The commit the implementer subagent made for Task 2 (e7dd1cf) has no blank line before the Co-Authored-By trailer, so git treats the trailer as part of the subject line. The controller noticed and recorded it as a deferred minor item instead of fixing it.
src/b.sh was committed without a shebang and with mode 100644. The reviewer deferred this as minor.
Codex is not on this host, so the Codex gates ran as no-ops. The agent said so clearly.

The session log moved partway through the run to a new project directory named for the worktree path (..--claude-worktrees-feature-parallel-6ba3c913). The original project dir has no JSONL, which could confuse tools that collect logs.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development via Skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". In the session log's tool_use list it is the first tool call, ahead of using-git-worktrees and every Bash call.

criteria.criterion: Ran sdd-state register and sdd-state next; next names Task 2 claimable
criteria.evidence: Log Bash commands: ".../sdd-state register docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 6ba3c913-... --integration feature/parallel" -> "status=registered integration=feature/parallel". Then ".../sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 6ba3c913-..." -> "status=next tasks=2 own-blocked=none plan=1a6af3e".

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with sdd-state claim ... 2 --session and worked it; ledger has Task 2: branch line
criteria.evidence: Log Bash command: "sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session 6ba3c913-05e8-4add-8d4b-c3681e374136" -> "status=claimed task=2 branch=feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from=46be16d". progress.md line 19: "Task 2: branch feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from 46be16d". Later lines read "Task 2: merged e7dd1cf into feature/parallel" and "Task 2: complete".

I listed every Bash tool_use command from the session JSONL with jq and grepped for 'takeover': 0 matches. The only '--takeover' text in the log is inside the loaded skill's own text. The final message says "I won't take over Task 1 unless you explicitly say so."

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: The log goes straight from the `next` output ("status=next tasks=2") through the pre-flight scan and snapshot to the claim of Task 2. The agent's text messages in that stretch only cover the worktree guard and Codex, with no question or hand-back about Task 1. No question came to me at all, so I never had to give a takeover answer.
